references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the healing of Peter's mother-in-law, where Jesus touched her hand, the fever left her, and she got up and served him.
Mark's parallel account of the healing of Peter's mother-in-law, where Jesus took her by the hand and raised her up, and the fever left her and she served them.
Shortly before this event, Jesus rebuked an unclean spirit and commanded it to come out, showing the same pattern where Jesus rebukes (ἐπετίμησεν) sickness and evil spirits with authority.
Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit with authority; the same Greek word (ἐπετίμησεν) is used as in Luke 4:39, demonstrating Jesus' authority over both evil spirits and sickness.
Jesus rebukes (ἐπετίμησεν) the wind and waves, showing his sovereign power to command natural forces, just as he rebuked the fever in 4:39.
Jesus rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Be still!", illustrating the same pattern of rebuking (ἐπετίμησεν) natural forces with divine authority.
Jairus' daughter got up immediately (παραχρῆμα) when Jesus commanded it, and she was told to be given food – parallel to the immediate healing and resumption of daily activities.
Mary served (διηκόνει) Jesus at the meal, using the same verb as for Peter's mother-in-law after her healing, showing grateful service in response to Jesus' presence.
Jesus rebukes (ἐπετίμησεν) the wind and sea, demonstrating his authority to command natural forces, parallel to his rebuke of the fever.
